channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: SpaceX seeks access to 80,000 US cell sites for wireless network: report
item.description: SpaceX is in talks with cellular infrastructure companies to secure access to at least 80,000 sites across the United States, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Microsoft develops AI tool that can diagnose 'sequentially' like a doctor
item.description: Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science.

item.title: FinTech M&A outlook improves, but investors remain selective on valuations: Report
item.description: Valuations of fintech companies have come under pressure across several segments as investors reassess businesses, while global fintech deal activity is showing signs of renewed momentum entering the fourth quarter of 2026, according to a report by D.A. Davidson.

item.title: iPhone Duo's entire first week stock pre-booked in India
item.description: Apple Store in BKC (Bandra Kurla Complex), Mumbai, and Saket, New Delhi, have clocked maximum number of pre-bookings for the ultra premium first foldable iPhone from the company's stable.

item.title: Rush is on to patch a software vulnerability that could impact 70% of websites worldwide
item.description: Many government sites appeared to be functioning normally Thursday, but outages or limited service continued while security work was under way.

item.title: Swiggy narrows loss in Q2; eMudhra cofounder on what went wrong
item.description: Happy Friday! Swiggy reported a rise in revenue in Q2 FY27 while cutting its losses. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: Steep bill for AI buildout punishes Meta, other tech favorites
item.description: Investors sold shares of Meta Platforms and a wealth of companies central to the AI trade, a day after Meta -- one of the so-called hyperscalers spending billions to build data centers and other infrastructure supporting the AI boom -- said it would issue a new class of shares that will help it raise funds.

item.title: Rhode Island sues Meta over alleged tolerance for scam advertising
item.description: The suit, filed by Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha in Providence Superior Court, accuses Meta of unlawfully profiting from and participating in the creation of billions of dollars in scam advertising - even as it assured its billions of users that it was working diligently to protect them.

item.title: Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety says rival Blinkit has the stronger flywheel, aims to fix basics before expanding
item.description: He said Swiggy’s priority is a stable business with “the clearest line of sight to Ebitda zero,” and that it would not use its cash reserves to open new fronts simply because the money is available. “I think our first job is to build a stable, resilient business that has the clearest line of sight to EBITDA zero. The optionalities come after that,” he said on the call following the announcement of the company's September quarter results.

item.title: BlueStone reports Rs 4.4 crore loss in Q2 as operating revenue rises 45%
item.description: The company’s operating revenue rose 45% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 745 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 513.6 crore a year earlier. Including other income of Rs 24.4 crore, BlueStone's total income stood at Rs 769 crore during the quarter.

item.title: Bridging the AI production gap: Over 100,000 Indian engineers trained to build with Gemini
item.description: India is seeing a significant shift in its technology workforce towards enterprise AI integration and solutions. The Build with Gemini initiative has trained over 100,000 developers and architects across several major organizations. This transition emphasizes the need for professionals skilled in engineering AI for production. Global System Integrators are crucial in facilitating this workforce transformation. The evolution aims to position India as a key player in AI architecture and engineering.

item.title: What is the PHP security vulnerability: The AI-found bug that made governments take websites offline
Anthropic unveils Claude Duet AI agent app
item.description: Anthropic on Thursday unveiled Claude Duet, a standalone AI agent app designed to act as a proactive assistant for professionals and small-business owners, as rivals such as OpenAI and Meta race to develop AI agents that can complete work autonomously on users' behalf.

item.title: Cognizant acquires DyFlex Solutions to enhance AI and SAP transformation capabilities
item.description: Cognizant Technology Solutions has signed an agreement to acquire DyFlex Solutions, enhancing its AI and SAP capabilities. This acquisition is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. DyFlex specializes in SAP transformation and is based in Australia and New Zealand. The deal marks Cognizant’s third acquisition in 2026 as it seeks to expand its services.

item.title: Swiggy to shift to inventory model starting Q3 FY27, eyes 80 bps Instamart margin boost
item.description: The transition is likely to improve its quick commerce arm Instamart’s contribution margin by around 80 basis points once fully implemented. It will also give the Bengaluru-based company better control over assortment, pricing, product availability, and day-to-day operations.

item.title: IBM falls as analysts question staying power of software rebound
item.description: IBM shares fell 6.5% in premarket trading on Thursday, as analysts said part of the company's third-quarter software rebound was driven by deals delayed from the previous quarter, raising questions about how sustainable the boost would be.

item.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business after controversy
item.description: Digital trust services provider eMudhra on Thursday said that it would voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business, following an incident where its certificates were found to have vulnerabilities.

item.title: Motilal Oswal entities apply for 2.39 crore Ola Electric shares in Rs 1,000-crore rights issue
item.description: Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors have put in their bids for shares in Ola Electric Mobility's latest rights issue, which is set to raise Rs 1,000 crore by offering partly paid-up shares at Rs 27 each. The rights issue commenced on Thursday and will conclude on October 30, with crucial payment details outlined.

item.title: eMudhra breach: Netizens react as IT Ministry says impact on Indian sites ‘very limited’
item.description: Cybersecurity agency CERT-In warned that the compromised keys could let attackers issue fraudulent certificates for domains they do not control, impersonate legitimate websites and carry out attacks that intercept or modify encrypted communications.

item.title: Cloudflare sees millions of exploit attempts after PHP disclosure
item.description: Cloud services firm Cloudflare saw millions of exploitation attempts after the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language PHP, CEO Matthew

item.title: Epic's 'Fortnite' back on Apple App Store in Australia after antitrust ruling
item.description: Epic Games said its shooter title "Fortnite" will return to Apple's App Store in Australia on Thursday after a federal court ordered the iPhone maker to open up its iOS operating system, having found it violated competition law.

item.title: Meta beats expectations but legal penalties hit profit amid AI race
item.description: Meta beat investor expectations for third-quarter revenue on Wednesday as it doubles down on a global AI race but the social media giant's profits took a hit due to an $18 billion legal settlement with nearly all US states. The company reported $9.86 billion in profits from July to September, almost 50 percent below investor expectations, which Meta said was dragged down by a $9.9 billion charge related to the settlement.

item.title: X Community Notes 'failed' to flag US election falsehoods, study says
item.description: A crowd-sourced verification system used by Elon Musk's X failed to flag a vast majority of false claims related to the US midterm elections -- including those promoted by the billionaire -- a study said Wednesday. "X's crowdsourced fact-checking program failed to flag 93.1 percent of false claims related to the US midterm elections," NewsGuard said.

item.title: Tesla aims to sell Cybercab robotaxis by end of year despite federal probe
item.description: Tesla is aiming to start selling its Cybercab robotaxis to the public by the end of this year, its engineering chief said on Wednesday, even as the US auto safety agency probes the vehicles that come without manual controls which federal regulations

item.title: DeepSeek wrapping up $15 billion fundraising to fuel AI race
item.description: Battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) and WeChat operator Tencent Holdings were among the biggest investors in the round, said one of the people, who both declined to be named as the information was confidential.

item.title: Government websites in Europe, US go dark over AI-detected flaw in a web programming language PHP
item.description: The website of the Finnish government, for one, was only partly available Wednesday. A message to visitors said government websites were experiencing a temporary disruption and were fully or partially unavailable while the issue was being resolved.

item.title: Meta strikes deal to keep Mark Zuckerberg in California after wealth tax concerns
item.description: By Carlos Me- Meta Platforms has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him living in California after the CEO warned he was considering leaving the state that houses the

item.title: Meta sued in Australia class action over alleged social media harm to children
item.description: A class action lawsuit has been filed in an Australia court against Meta Platforms' Facebook and Instagram, alleging the social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them addictive through algorithms.

item.title: Walmart launches tools for AI agents to shop for customers
item.description: Walmart on Wednesday intrduced new tools that will allow artificial intelligence agents to shop and complete transactions for customers, as the retailer seeks to position itself in the growing use of AI-powered assistants in online commerce.

item.title: Anthropic, music publishers square off on 'fair use' defense in AI copyright case
item.description: US District Judge Eumi Lee did not rule at a hearing in San Jose but pressed both sides on the fair use question, which could be key to dozens of other high-stakes copyright infringement cases in the AI era.

item.title: Chinese-linked hackers compromise ConnectWise, target hundreds in global attack, Microsoft says
item.description: A Chinese-linked hacking group used an AI-driven penetration testing tool to compromise IT services firm ConnectWise as part of a campaign that targeted hundreds of organizations globally, Microsoft said on Wednesday.

item.title: Eternal’s strong Q2 report; Exits outpace hiring at top IT firms
item.description: Happy Thursday! Eternal’s Q2 revenue surged on Blinkit’s growth. This and more in today’s ETtech Morning Dispatch.

item.title: OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation
item.description: OpenAI's safety practices have been in the spotlight in recent months, after the company said a swarm of its AI agents escaped containment and hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face. OpenAI President Greg Brockman was among the group of six tech executives who later signed US President Donald Trump's voluntary AI safety agreement on behalf of their companies, agreeing to work with "independent auditors" and to ensure their AI tools do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways."

item.title: Europe's financial regulators query Google over cloud outage that hit banks
item.description: The European Banking Authority said that it has been in contact with Google Cloud to obtain further information on the incident, understand its implications and assess its potential impact on financial entities in the EU, a spokesperson for the watchdog told Reuters.

item.title: Nvidia's Huang hails Europe's AI potential, flanked by robot ducks
item.description: In a demonstration of Europe's AI creativity, Huang shared the stage with tiny duck-shaped, AI-trained robots developed by French startup Pollen Robotics in collaboration with Hugging Face, asking them to perform somersaults.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay New Mexico $25 billion after jury finds it deceived Facebook users about privacy
item.description: Jurors in September found Meta liable for over 43 million violations of New Mexico consumer protection laws when a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, harvested Facebook user data to generate targeted political ads for the 2016 election.

item.title: Vulnerable keys were created but never put to commercial use, investigation on: eMudhra cofounder
item.description: eMudhra issues digital signature and website security certificates to enable them securely connect to browsers for public access. "There's no impact to subscribers because we have done all the actions. We are also working with our customers to notify them that there is no impact because no certificates were issued. This does not affect our other lines of business, which is the India digital signature and our enterprise solutions business," eMudhra co-founder Kaushik Srinivasan told PTI.

item.title: Cryptocurrency companies can keep paying interest-like rewards, say federal bank regulators
item.description: The new rules are part of the implementation of the GENIUS Act, which was signed into law last year and was meant to codify the rules and regulations around issuers of stablecoins.

item.title: Explained: What is PHP and why did it take government websites offline?
item.description: The developers of PHP said on Wednesday they would release patches for two critical vulnerabilities, and EU cybersecurity officials warned organisations unable to apply the fixes to take affected websites offline. Here is what you need to know:

item.title: EBay to lay off 9% of workforce in push to simplify operations
item.description: EBay will lay off about 1,000 employees, representing 9% of its workforce, to streamline operations. The company previously reduced its staff by 800 positions in February to improve efficiency. EBay is focusing on authenticated luxury goods, collectibles, and refurbished products, which have attracted higher-paying consumers. The recent acquisition of fashion resale platform Depop has also strengthened eBay's market position. EBay plans to report its latest earnings next week.

item.title: Special team to probe eMudhra incident; impact on Indian websites, applications very limited: Govt
item.description: The ministry said the reported security incident pertains to eMudhra’s global certificate business, and its impact on Indian websites is very limited.It also said some social media accounts were indulging in fear-mongering about the impact.

item.title: Deepinder Goyal’s Temple to open pre-orders on November 1
item.description: Temple is a head-worn device that tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. Goyal, who stepped down as Eternal CEO in February, had said in August that pre-orders for a limited launch edition would open soon.

item.title: Blinkit sees no compelling case for expanding private labels, says Dhindsa
item.description: Albinder Dhindsa, CEO of Eternal, voiced skepticism regarding the potential for private labels to enhance profit margins. He emphasised that effective brand development mandates considerable investment in both marketing and product development, areas where Blinkit falls short.

item.title: Glance to be integrated by default on Android TVs in US, India, Japan in partnership with Google
item.description: Under the collaboration, Glance will transform idle TV screens into interactive shoppable storefronts across fashion, travel, food, wellness, and other lifestyle categories.

item.title: Dark Matter: Eternal’s chatbot will keep user conversations private even from the company — Deepinder Goyal
item.description: In a letter to shareholders, Goyal explained the idea behind Dark was to remove the worry that someone, someday, can read what you tell an AI bot. “All of us have a dark side, and it needs an outlet where it doesn’t have to hide,” he wrote.

item.title: Einride expands Nvidia partnership to deploy AI reasoning model for self-driving trucks
item.description: Self-driving truck company Einride said on Wednesday it would broaden its partnership with Nvidia by testing the chipmaker's AI reasoning model, Alpamayo, in its self-driving vehicles, aiming to speed up the expansion of autonomous freight services while lowering development costs

item.title: Booking.com targeted in EU investigation into phishing scams, fraudulent listings
item.description: The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition enforcer, said it opened an investigation following a preliminary probe and after analysing risk assessment reports submitted by Booking.com this year and the previous three years.

item.title: Eternal Q2 Results: Profit soars 92% YoY to Rs 125 crore; revenue zooms 78%
item.description: Eternal Q2 Results: Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, reported a 92.3% year-on-year (YoY) jump in net profit to Rs 125 crore in the second quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 65 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.

item.title: China's Moonshot AI to operate in Singapore, jobs post shows
item.description: Chinese AI startup Moonshot is expanding into Singapore, with a new sales role listed on the company's LinkedIn page this week.

item.title: OpenAI says its AI agents weakened internal monitoring system
item.description: By Carlos Me- OpenAI said on Tuesday that two of its AI agents weakened parts of an internal monitoring system designed to detect misbehavior, the latest case of AI agents acting in ways their developers did not intend them to.
